claims.claim: PACCAR Parts reached record quarterly revenue of $1.75 billion in Q2 2026, supported by a global distribution network and installed truck base.
PACCAR continues investing in clean diesel, hybrid and battery-electric powertrains, connected vehicle services and manufacturing capability.

factors.name: aftermarket resilience
factors.basis: Record parts revenue provides a recurring installed-base complement to cyclical new-truck sales.

factors.name: powertrain transition optionality
factors.basis: Investment across multiple propulsion paths preserves optionality but requires capital and technology execution.

risks.risk: Heavy-truck demand remains cyclical and sensitive to freight economics, fleet replacement and macro conditions.

unknowns.unknown: Economic returns from next-generation powertrain and connected-service investments are not separately quantified here.

claims.claim: PACCAR Q2 2026 net income was $752 million, up 24% from the preceding quarter, on $7.55 billion of consolidated net sales and financial-services revenue.
Global truck deliveries were 38,700 units and management linked higher build rates to strong orders and improving freight rates.
2026 capital expenditures are projected at $700-$750 million and R&D at $450-$480 million.

factors.name: cyclical execution
factors.basis: Sequential profit improvement and higher build rates indicate current demand conversion.

factors.name: capital discipline
factors.basis: Substantial capex and R&D support future technology but require returns through a cyclical market.

risks.risk: Improved freight conditions can reverse; current build-rate strength should not be extrapolated indefinitely.

unknowns.unknown: Scout does not convert current truck-cycle evidence into a valuation or numeric score.
